cases.name: Endpoint health check after deployment
cases.input: Check the health of our production endpoint after the latest deployment.
expected_behaviors: Runs az ml online-endpoint show to verify provisioningState is Succeeded
Runs az ml online-deployment show to check requestFailedCount vs requestSucceededCount
Retrieves recent deployment logs with az ml online-deployment get-logs
Reports failure rate as a percentage and flags if above 1%
Checks for OutOfMemoryError, ConnectionRefused, or Timeout in logs
should_not: Only check endpoint state without checking deployment health
Ignore deployment logs — errors may not show in endpoint status
Assume endpoint is healthy if provisioningState is Succeeded without checking request metrics

cases.name: Data drift detection on production features
cases.input: I want to check if there's data drift in our production features compared to the baseline.
expected_behaviors: Uses a production baseline (not training data) for comparison
Computes PSI for numeric features with threshold > 0.25 for warning
Computes KS test for numeric features with p-value < 0.05 for warning
Computes chi-squared test for categorical features
Reports per-feature drift metrics and flags features exceeding thresholds
should_not: Use training data as the baseline for drift detection
Only compute one drift metric — should use at least PSI and KS test
Ignore categorical features in drift analysis
Treat seasonal shifts as drift without considering seasonality

cases.name: Model performance drift investigation
cases.input: Our model predictions seem to have shifted in production. Investigate the drift.
expected_behaviors: Compares prediction distributions between baseline and current periods using PSI
Checks feature attribution drift using feature importance ranking correlation
Reports prediction mean shift and standard deviation ratio
Correlates prediction drift with feature drift to identify root cause
Recommends retraining if drift is sustained and performance degraded > 10%
should_not: Only check prediction distribution without checking feature drift
Recommend immediate retraining without confirming drift is sustained (> 2 weeks)
Ignore the possibility that upstream data changes caused the prediction shift

cases.name: Configure Azure ML monitoring schedule
cases.input: Set up automated data drift monitoring for our endpoint on a weekly schedule.
expected_behaviors: Creates a monitoring YAML with target dataset, baseline dataset, and drift thresholds
Uses az ml schedule create with the monitoring YAML
Configures a cron schedule (e.g., 0 0 * * 1 for weekly Monday)
Defines alert thresholds per the drift threshold table (PSI > 0.25, KS p-value < 0.05)
Confirms the schedule was created and is enabled
should_not: Use training data as the baseline dataset in the monitoring configuration
Set thresholds that are too sensitive (e.g., PSI > 0.05) causing constant false positives
Create the schedule without verifying the workspace has monitoring features enabled

cases.name: Production data quality check
cases.input: Check if there are any data quality issues in our production data — null rates, unexpected values.
expected_behaviors: Compares current null rates against baseline null rates with 1.5x increase threshold
Checks numeric columns for values outside expected min/max ranges
Reports per-column issues with actual vs expected values
Distinguishes between new-entity nulls (expected) and unexpected null increases
Provides actionable summary of which columns need investigation
should_not: Flag nulls for new entities as data quality issues without considering entity age
Only check null rates without checking value ranges
Report issues without providing actual vs expected values for context
